topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the cancer lecture series and outlines the key learning objectives regarding the causes of cancer.

topics.label: Etiological concepts, mutation sources, and epidemiological patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore what drives cancer development by comparing intrinsic mutational processes and inherited predispositions with environmental exposures and global epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents drive oncogenesis, focusing on oncogenic viral and bacterial mechanisms and the detailed etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the molecular mechanisms by which physical radiation and chemical carcinogens induce direct DNA damage, metabolic activation, or oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and contextual susceptibility in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic tumor promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental susceptibility interact with initial mutations to enable tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for detecting carcinogenicity and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental strategies used to identify carcinogens and evaluate human health risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture with a final recap of key themes and concluding remarks.
